guards: What "degrades deterministically" has to mean for the rerank stage, and the first case that pinned it: with the cross-encoder down the retriever must fall back to the RRF-fused order exactly, not to whichever half answered first. The fixture is built so the two differ - the dense half's top-ranked chunk fuses to last, because RRF rewards agreement across lists rather than depth in one - so replacing Fuse with a dense-first concatenation changes the retrieved order while every chunk is still present and every citation still resolves. It cannot see a sparse-first concatenation, which gives this fixture's fused order exactly, nor a merge on raw scores, which over fixture snippets that all score zero is that same concatenation; evidence-topk-degraded-rerank-fused-order-capped is built so both differ from RRF, and it is the case that catches them. Pairs with the sparse-half case: that one asserts the degradation was recorded, this one asserts what it degraded to.

evidence.intent: The reranker throws. Sparse ranks [warfarin-inr, acei-potassium] and dense ranks [doac-renal, warfarin-inr, acei-potassium], so the fused order is [warfarin-inr, acei-potassium, doac-renal] - the dense top-ranked chunk last, carried by one list alone. Asserts that exact order, the degraded stage set {rerank}, and the fallback warning in the log.
evidence.question: Testpatient Victor is on warfarin and lisinopril - summarise the monitoring the guidelines ask for.

corpus.text: For most patients with atrial fibrillation on warfarin, the target INR is 2.0 to 3.0.
When starting or up-titrating an ACE inhibitor or ARB, monitor serum potassium and creatinine within one to two weeks.
Direct oral anticoagulants require dose reduction or avoidance in renal impairment.
